test_title: PYST 39: Selection Post (Matric Level) - English Language (Held On 5 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Nirmala scored forty runs in the school cricket match.

options.text: Forty runs scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match.
Forty runs was being scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match.
Forty runs had been scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match.
Forty runs were scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match.

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To **convert the sentence** into passive voice, we **need** to make the object (forty runs) the subject of the sentence.
 
• Use the appropriate form of the verb **"to be" **(were) with the **past participle** of the main verb (scored).

Therefore, the **correct passive sentence **is: * "Forty runs were scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forty runs scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match. -** This is **not in passive voice **but rather a rearranged form of the active sentence.
 
• **Forty runs was being scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match. -** The use of **"was being scored" **implies ongoing action, which does not fit the context of a single cricket match.
 
• **Forty runs had been scored by Nirmala in the school cricket match. - **The use of **"had been scored"** indicates a past action that happened before another past action, which is not necessary in this sentence. The simple past tense "were scored" is sufficient.
